title: Fix qh2: state what happens at the 20-roll cap
summary: qh2 is ill-posed: its text calls the value infinite, then caps the game at 20 rolls without saying what is paid if no 6 appears. The stored answer ($13,675) silently drops the 2.6% of games with no 6. This rewrite states the cap and pays $2^20 in that case.

question.title: Doubling Until a Six, Capped
question.description: You roll a fair die until a 6 appears, but the game stops after at most 20 rolls. If the first 6 comes on roll n, you're paid $2ⁿ. If no 6 appears in 20 rolls, you're paid $2²⁰. What is your expected payout? Round to the nearest dollar.
question.explanation: Each extra roll doubles the payout but happens with probability 5/6, so the terms grow by 5/3 per roll: without a cap the expected value is infinite. With the cap, two-thirds of the value ($27,351) comes from the 2.6% of games that never see a 6, so the expectation is dominated by rare outcomes.

reasoningPattern: Expected value of a truncated game: a geometric series plus the tail case.

sources.note: Same game and cap; the no-6 case is now stated
General idea of a doubling payout with infinite expectation; wording and numbers here are original

authenticity.rationale: Doubling payouts and infinite expectations are a common interview theme, but asking for a figure to the dollar turns it into a calculation. An interviewer would more likely ask whether you would pay to play and why rare outcomes dominate; this version keeps the bank's numeric format.

openQuestions: The answer changes from 13,675 to 41,026. Approve the rewrite, or would you rather mark qh2 inactive?
